subject: Tenant data transfer evidence & subprocessor clarity for Yarrow Health
messages:
From: Contracting Team <contracting@yarrowhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@yarrowhealth.com
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence request — tenant-level transfer records + subprocessor certifications

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal and our DPO have a few follow-ups before we can clear the vendor review: specifically we need an extract of Article 30-style processing activities that show the transfer/legal basis for tenant-level data flows (the ledger can be redacted at the PII level but must show destination, legal mechanism, and date ranges).

Separately, they asked for a current subprocessor certification matrix (ISO/SOC attestation + last audit date) for any subprocessors that could store or process tenant data, and confirmation on whether any KMS keys are customer-controlled or hosted in-region for EU tenants.

Can you share a timeline for these items? If possible can we also get a short DPIA summary for the Yarrow tenant that calls out residual risk and any compensating controls?

Best,
Erin Walsh
Contracts & Procurement
Yarrow Health

Attachment: request-checklist.xlsx (stub)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Contracting Team <contracting@yarrowhealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, procurement@yarrowhealth.com
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request — tenant-level transfer records + subprocessor certifications

Hi Erin — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (Privacy lead) and Rishi (Legal) to scope what we can provide right away and what will require a brief review.

Quick notes up front:
- We can produce an Article 30-style ledger extract that shows processing activities, destinations, and the transfer mechanism (SCCs or in-region hosting), redacting tenant PII as requested.
- We maintain an up-to-date subprocessor matrix; Marissa will attach the cert matrix and indicate which subprocessors store tenant data vs. those used for infra/observability.
- KMS: for hosted customers we use Redwood-managed keys by default; customers can opt for BYOK in Dedicated/Private. We will confirm region specifics for EU tenants.
- DPIA summary: we have a concise DPIA support summary template that we can fill for Yarrow; it will include residual risk and mitigations.

Can you confirm the files of interest are: (1) Article 30 ledger excerpt, (2) subprocessor certification matrix, (3) short DPIA summary, and (4) confirmation on KMS region/BYOK option? If yes, we'll aim to deliver a draft package by end of day (PST) tomorrow and share a DocuSign link for a non-disclosure addendum if Yarrow needs the unredacted ledger.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Head of Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

--
Olga Petrov
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0134
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Contracting Team <contracting@yarrowhealth.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, procurement@yarrowhealth.com
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request — tenant-level transfer records + subprocessor certifications

Hi Erin — thanks, and hi Olga/Rishi. Attaching the initial package below.

What's included in this submission (attached as redacted stubs):
1) redwood_article30_register_excerpt.pdf — ledger extract showing processing categories, destination country, transfer mechanism, and first/last observed transfer dates. PII columns replaced with tenant_id hashes.
2) subprocessor_cert_matrix.csv — current inventory with ISO/SOC attestation status, last audit date, and which subprocessors may have access to tenant artifacts (storage, logs, KV caches).
3) dpia-summary-yarrow-tenant-2027-07-29.docx — our DPIA support summary for Yarrow that outlines data flows, identified risks, and compensating controls (KV cache TTL, prefix-caching exclusions, anonymization guidance).

KMS note: for the Yarrow EU tenant we confirm primary keys are hosted in the eu-west-1 region with Redwood-managed keys by default. If you require BYOK we support a Dedicated/Private deployment pattern and can provide an onboarding playbook; I'll include a short note in the DPIA.

A couple of clarifying questions for your DPO so we can finalize:
- Does the DPO require the ledger to include event-level timestamps per transfer, or are date ranges sufficient?
- Are SOC2 Type II reports sufficient for the attestation column, or do you need raw audit reports/management letters for any specific subprocessors?

We can put unredacted extracts behind a DocuSign NDA (link below) or provide a secure transient Drive link with limited access — whichever works best for your team.

Attachments: redwood_article30_register_excerpt.pdf (stub), subprocessor_cert_matrix.csv (stub), dpia-summary-yarrow-tenant-2027-07-29.docx (stub)
Related link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cREDWOOD-article30-excerpt
DocuSign placeholder: https://app.docusign.com/transactions/ABCD1234

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if the DPO prefers.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Erin Walsh <contracting@yarrowhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: DPO <dpo@yarrowhealth.com>, procurement@yarrowhealth.com
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request — tenant-level transfer records + subprocessor certifications

Marissa — thanks for the thorough package, looks close to what we need. A few quick items from our DPO:

- Date granularity: date ranges are fine for initial review; we'll request event-level timestamps only for a narrow sample if needed during security assessment.
- Attestation: SOC2 Type II is generally acceptable; for three subprocessors that access logs we will ask for the management letters — will flag those by name in a follow-up once we confirm.
- DocuSign NDA: please send the NDA link for the unredacted ledger excerpts. Procurement will review the DPIA summary and follow up on BYOK costs if we decide to pursue Dedicated.

Can we have the NDA and the secure unredacted extract link by EOD tomorrow? Also please confirm whether the subprocessor matrix includes the last penetration test date for infra providers — that's helpful for our risk team.

Appreciate the quick turnaround,
Erin Walsh
Contracts & Procurement
Yarrow Health
